question: According to the MUTCD, what exact percentage reduction in crashes is guaranteed by installing a STOP sign or all-way stop control?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not state any percentage reduction in crashes—guaranteed or otherwise—from installing a STOP sign or all-way stop control. The evidence provided contains no such figure; instead, it addresses crash-frequency thresholds and other conditions used to justify *considering* or *permitting* stop control. The premise of the question is not supported by the MUTCD text. Guidance (recommended): - Minor-road stop control should be considered when engineering judgment indicates conditions such as restricted view, crash records (e.g., for a four-leg intersection, three or more reported crashes in a 12-month period or six or more in a 36-month period, susceptible to correction by minor-road stop control), functional classification differences, or when conditions supporting all-way stop control no longer exist. This describes when stop control should be considered—not any guaranteed crash reduction. Options (permitted): - All-way stop control may be installed where an engineering study indicates specified crash experience (e.g., five or more reported crashes in 12 months at a four-leg intersection, of a type susceptible to correction by all-way stop control)—again a threshold for consideration, not a promised reduction. - All-way stop control may also be installed based on inadequate sight distance, as an interim measure pending signal or roundabout yield control, or based on 8-hour combined vehicle/pedestrian/bicycle volumes; none of these provisions cite any crash-reduction percentage. Citations: - Section 2B.11 Guidance §1 (p.78) - Section 2B.13 Option §1 (p.79) - Section 2B.14 Option §1 (p.79) - Section 2B.15 Option §1 (p.79) - Section 2B.16 Option §1 (p.79)
